clue.text: No details matter (anag.).

indicators.note: the bracketed note 'anag.' tells the solver outright that the preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrug of indifference: the small points are unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue: the fodder is the whole clue and the bracketed 'anag.' is the indicator; the phrase also suggests ragged folk who care nothing for the details of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged, unkempt people are scruffs who plainly pay no heed to the finer points of their appearance.

clue.text: Relating to current events and containing large type.

definitions.text: Relating to current events and containing large type.

parts.words: Relating to current events and containing large type
parts.note: a word about the news of the day which holds within it the name of a printing type size

explanation.surface: A newspaper's front page: news of the day set in big headline type.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue only says the answer contains PICA (a type size); the surrounding TO...L are not clued separately, as often in early puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical concerns matters of present interest, the news of the day.

clue.text: Inns, but the vat has been turned upside down!

definitions.text: Inns, but the vat has been turned upside down!

parts.words: Inns, but the vat has been turned upside down
parts.note: drinking houses whose name opens with the word vat written backwards, as if the barrel were upended

explanation.surface: A rowdy night at the inn ends with the beer barrel knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer begins TAV, which is VAT turned round; the rest of the word is not clued.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are public houses where drink is sold, a synonym for inns.

clue.text: Fashion's reversed in an Eastern land.

indicators.note: reversed tells us the word for fashion is to be written back to front

parts.note: fashion is mode (the 's is 'is', a link)

explanation.surface: Western styles are turned upside down in some Oriental country.
explanation.definitionFit: Edom was an ancient biblical kingdom south of the Dead Sea, in the Near East.

clue.text: One of these is supreme in 13.

definitions.text: One of these is supreme in 13.

parts.words: One of these is supreme in 13
parts.note: 13 across is a great church, whose chief cleric heads its chapter

explanation.surface: Someone holds the top post in a certain institution.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference to 13 across, MINSTER: the head of a minster's chapter is its dean.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is the senior clergyman presiding over a cathedral or collegiate church.

clue.text: Behead this watch word, and a fragrant oil remains.

definitions.text: Behead this watch word, and a fragrant oil remains.

parts.words: Behead this watch word, and a fragrant oil remains
parts.note: a slogan which, with its first letter cut off, leaves otto, the perfume oil also called attar

explanation.surface: A grim execution scene in which only a sweet scent lingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter M and OTTO (attar of roses) is left; 'watch word' is split to look like a word about a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchword is a rallying slogan or maxim, which is what a motto is.

clue.text: Behold the Inland Revenue and retreat!

parts.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
IR is the abbreviation for the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax office

explanation.surface: Seeing the taxman coming, one flees in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the British tax authority, abbreviated IR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den or hiding place, somewhere an animal or person retreats to.

clue.text: The end of this young tree's a fish.

definitions.text: The end of this young tree's a fish.

parts.words: The end of this young tree's a fish
parts.note: a sapling whose name finishes in ling, a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An odd nature note claiming a sapling turns into a fish at its tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is OAK plus LING; the last four letters spell a fish, so the clue leans on the tree's name rather than building it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oakling is a young oak, a small tree just starting out.

clue.text: While doing it for your seat at the coronation you may fail to do it.

definitions.text: While doing it for your seat at the coronation you may fail to do it.

parts.words: While doing it for your seat at the coronation you may fail to do it
parts.note: hunting for your place, you may miss sight of the monarch

explanation.surface: A spectator at a royal crowning hunts for a seat and misses the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'do it' is the whole word (looking for); the second is the word split in two, SEE KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking means searching or looking for something, here one's allotted seat.

clue.text: "But 0, she dances such way" might have been said of her.

definitions.text: "But 0, she dances such way" might have been said of her.

parts.words: But 0, she dances such way" might have been said of her
parts.note: a line from Suckling's Ballad upon a Wedding, fitting a celebrated Russian ballerina

explanation.surface: A quotation of admiration for a graceful dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is from Sir John Suckling ('But O, she dances such a way!'); the zero is the printed O. It suits Anna Pavlova, the great ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Pavlova was the most famous ballerina of her age, celebrated for her grace.

clue.text: Roman road found in Belgravia.

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the next word

explanation.surface: An archaeological find: traces of a Roman road under a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Belgravia is an upmarket district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Via is the Latin word for road, as in the Via Appia.

clue.text: A little shell-fish after tea makes a quivering movement.

indicators.note: after places the shellfish behind the letter for tea

parts.note: tea is sounded as the letter T
a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A seafood tea-time leaves someone with a shudder.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinkle is a brief flicker or tremor, as of light or an eye.

clue.text: A — sheet and a flowing sea.

definitions.text: A — sheet and a flowing sea.

parts.words: A — sheet and a flowing sea
parts.note: fill the gap in Allan Cunningham's sea song, which opens with a damp sail

explanation.surface: A line of seafaring verse with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cunningham's song begins 'A wet sheet and a flowing sea'; the sheet is a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet soaked by spray is damp, the word the poem uses for it.

clue.text: If I left this church and you entered it the result would be Irish.

definitions.text: If I left this church and you entered it the result would be Irish.

parts.words: If I left this church and you entered it the result would be Irish
parts.note: swap the letter I for the letter U in a word for a great church and you get Munster, an Irish province

explanation.surface: A sectarian quip about changing churches and becoming Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' and 'you' are the letters I and U: replace I by U and MUNSTER, the Irish province, results.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large church, originally one attached to a monastery.

clue.text: These lions are tame enough to be kept in the kitchen.

definitions.text: These lions are tame enough to be kept in the kitchen.

parts.words: These lions are tame enough to be kept in the kitchen
parts.note: kitchen drudges whose name ends in the word lions

explanation.surface: A circus joke about big cats docile enough for domestic service.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer ends in LIONS but means kitchen servants.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a lowly kitchen servant who washed dishes and pots.

clue.text: This sort of horse would hardly win at 18.

definitions.text: This sort of horse would hardly win at 18.

parts.words: This sort of horse would hardly win at 18
parts.note: a heavy draught animal would be no use at the racecourse at 18 across

explanation.surface: A racing tip warning against a particular sort of runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is ASCOT, the royal racecourse in Berkshire; a carthorse is bred for pulling, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A carthorse is a strong, slow draught horse used for hauling loads.

clue.text: As I need (anag.).

indicators.note: the bracketed note 'anag.' tells the solver outright that the preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stating a requirement.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue with no definition: the bracketed 'anag.' signals that 'As I need' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearranged phrase gives the name of a liquorice-flavoured seed used in cooking and drinks.

clue.text: A: little bird becomes a giant, and then a fairy queen

definitions.text: A: little bird becomes a giant, and then a fairy queen

parts.words: A: little bird becomes a giant, and then a fairy queen
parts.note: a small bird plus letters grows into one of the giant gods of Greek myth, and grows again into Oberon's consort

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale transformation from tiny bird to giant to queen.
explanation.walkthrough: TIT (little bird) grows to TITAN (a giant) and then to TITANIA, queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: In brief, a Caledonian.

parts.note: an indefinite article run together with a word for a native of Scotland, said in short

explanation.surface: A short description of somebody from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Caledonia is the old name for Scotland; 'a Scot' run together gives the racecourse (and a cravat).
explanation.definitionFit: Run together, the phrase names the royal racecourse and a broad neck scarf.

clue.text: Is in backward except in Latin.

indicators.note: backward says the words 'Is in' are read right to left

explanation.surface: A grammar tip about an exception in Latin usage.
explanation.walkthrough: A decree nisi is a provisional order, 'unless' cause is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisi is the Latin word for unless, so it means except.

clue.text: Falls.

parts.note: a noun, as in a great waterfall, not a verb

explanation.surface: A single word that looks like a verb about tumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as a verb but is the noun: the famous cataract on the US-Canada border.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the best-known waterfall in North America, often called simply the Falls.

clue.text: Unlike those mentioned in 14.

parts.note: 14 down plays on kitchen staff; this creature is a big marine mammal, nothing like a tame servant

explanation.surface: A contrast drawn with an earlier group.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is SCULLIONS ('lions' kept in the kitchen); this beast is a wild seagoing 'lion' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lion is an eared seal, a large marine mammal with a lion-like roar.

clue.text: When confused, she naturally seems inane.

indicators.note: when confused says the letters of the word inane are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unkind remark that a muddled woman comes across as silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a female given name, so it fits a woman referred to as she.

clue.text: The Chinaman at the start recommends his laundry for this.

definitions.text: The Chinaman at the start recommends his laundry for this.

parts.words: The Chinaman at the start recommends his laundry for this
parts.note: a dated jibe at the laundryman's accent: his pitch begins with Li, a Chinese surname

explanation.surface: A laundryman touting for business.
explanation.walkthrough: An offensive period clue: the answer begins LI, a Chinese name, and is the cloth a laundry washes.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is fabric from flax, and household sheets and shirts are what a laundry washes.

clue.text: This after 39 is a recorder.

parts.note: 39 across is a girl's name; put this word behind it and you get a chronicler of yearly records

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a numbered instrument for keeping records.
explanation.walkthrough: 39 across is ANNA; ANNA + LIST is ANNALIST, one who records annals. 'Recorder' tempts toward the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a written record of items, and placed after ANNA it makes a chronicler.

clue.text: Cheese that starts by looking high and ends by looking heavy.

definitions.text: Cheese that starts by looking high and ends by looking heavy.

parts.words: Cheese that starts by looking high and ends by looking heavy
parts.note: a cheese whose name opens with a pole for walking raised up and closes with a unit of great weight, sharing a letter

explanation.surface: A cheese that seems lofty at first and ends weighty.
explanation.walkthrough: The name begins STILT (a pole that lifts you high) and ends TON (a great weight); the two share the middle T, so it cannot be a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a strong English blue-veined cheese.

clue.text: An old coin reversed and nothing backward make a citadel.

indicators.note: reversed says the coin's name is written back to front

parts.note: the merk was an old Scottish silver coin

indicators.note: backward says the word for nothing is turned right to left too

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Building a fortress by turning a coin and a blank about.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified citadel at the heart of Moscow, and kremlin means a Russian citadel generally.

clue.text: A delicate walker makes a music-hall joke.

definitions.meaning: the Amalekite king in 1 Samuel 15 who came to Samuel 'delicately'
a gag is a comedian's joke, preceded by the article

explanation.surface: A dainty-stepping comedian gets a laugh on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel the captured king 'came unto him delicately'; split, the name reads A GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Agag is the biblical king who walked delicately, and split it is a comic's joke.

clue.text: Rebel of old, but now, no doubt, a loyal mason.

definitions.meaning: Wat ... led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
the doorkeeper of a Freemasons' lodge has this title

explanation.surface: A historic rebel whose descendants are now loyal citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Freemasons' lodge doorkeeper is the tyler; the surface's 'but now' contrasts rebellion with loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat Tyler led the 1381 revolt, and the doorkeeper guarding a Masonic lodge bears the same title.

clue.text: A showy plant, pruned at the end, becomes foot soldier in India.

indicators.note: pruned at the end says the flower's name loses its last letter

parts.note: the peony is a garden plant with big showy blooms

explanation.surface: A gardener's peony is cut back and turns into an Indian soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a peon was a foot soldier, attendant or messenger.

clue.text: Warm garment covering Ena and Paul.

indicators.note: covering here wraps the two names into one garment, rearranging their letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cosy cloak big enough to wrap a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' is the loose signal that the letters of Ena and Paul are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A paenula was a heavy hooded Roman cloak worn against cold and rain.

clue.text: What you have this you should pay for.

definitions.text: What you have this you should pay for.

parts.words: What you have this you should pay for
parts.note: anything requested from a shop or waiter must be paid for

explanation.surface: A moral maxim about settling one's bills.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'what you have requested you should pay for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that have been requested from a supplier are ordered, and owe payment.

clue.text: Lover whom a one-eyed rival crushed beneath a rock.

definitions.text: Lover whom a one-eyed rival crushed beneath a rock.

parts.words: Lover whom a one-eyed rival crushed beneath a rock
parts.note: Galatea's shepherd lover, killed by the jealous Cyclops Polyphemus

explanation.surface: A grisly love triangle ended with a boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Ovid, the Cyclops Polyphemus (one-eyed) crushed Galatea's beloved under a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Acis was the young shepherd loved by the nymph Galatea and killed by Polyphemus.

clue.text: Mixed bathing which included these would be too mixed.

definitions.text: Mixed bathing which included these would be too mixed.

parts.words: Mixed bathing which included these would be too mixed
parts.note: large sea eels sharing the water with swimmers would make the company too varied

explanation.surface: A prim remark on men and women swimming together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed bathing' meant men and women together; adding big eels would take mixing too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Congers are large marine eels, not welcome companions for swimmers.

clue.text: There's an obvious snag in this Dickens character.

definitions.text: There's an obvious snag in this Dickens character.

parts.words: There's an obvious snag in this Dickens character
parts.note: a figure from Bleak House whose name opens with the word snag

explanation.surface: A critic's complaint about a flaw in a Dickens creation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Snagsby is the law stationer in Bleak House; 'snag' is visibly in his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Snagsby is the timid law-stationer in Dickens's Bleak House.

clue.text: Miss Johnson's trip to Australia was this.

definitions.text: Miss Johnson's trip to Australia was this.

parts.words: Miss Johnson's trip to Australia was this
parts.note: Amy Johnson flew solo from England to Australia in 1930

explanation.surface: A newsy reference to a famous aviator's long-distance journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy Johnson made the first solo flight by a woman from England to Australia in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerial means taking place in the air, as a flight does.

clue.text: This runaway slave is brownish crimson.

definitions.meaning: a fugitive slave in the West Indies, from Spanish cimarrón

explanation.surface: A description of a fugitive's complexion or clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both escaped West Indian slaves and a dark red-brown colour.

clue.text: Ancient book of Scandinavia.

parts.note: the Old Norse collections of myth and poetry from medieval Iceland

explanation.surface: A plain description of an old Nordic text.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic compilation of Norse mythological poetry and lore.

clue.text: A twisted claw relates to sound.

indicators.note: twisted says the letters of the claw word are bent into a new order

parts.note: a talon is a bird's claw

explanation.surface: A bent claw has something to do with sound.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: the letters of TALON, not the clue's own words, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonal means concerning tone, the quality or pitch of a sound.

clue.text: Northern place of learning.

parts.note: the Manchester college founded on John ... bequest

explanation.surface: A plain reference to a college in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Owens College, Manchester, became the University of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Owens College in Manchester was a noted northern English seat of higher education.

clue.text: If you find this drug bitter, change it into a sole.

indicators.note: change it into tells us the letters of 'a sole' are rearranged to make the drug

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who dislikes a bitter medicine: turn it into fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the drug's letters rearrange into A SOLE, the flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloes is a bitter purgative drug made from aloe leaves.

clue.text: Christian name of 9.

indicators.note: of here means drawn out of, so the letters come from inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A query about someone's first name.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is PAVLOVA, whose first name was Anna; neatly, it also sits inside 'christiAN NAme', with 'of' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna was the given name of the ballerina Pavlova.

clue.text: One of the haunts of Ariel.

definitions.text: One of the haunts of Ariel.

parts.words: One of the haunts of Ariel
parts.note: Ariel sings in The Tempest 'In a ... bell I lie'

explanation.surface: A question about where a fairy spirit lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel's song in Shakespeare's The Tempest: 'Where the bee sucks, there suck I; in a cowslip's bell I lie.'
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a wild flower whose bell Ariel names as a resting place.

clue.text: Some coal ends in this.

parts.note: the purest hard coal finishes with this word, which itself means quote

explanation.surface: Coal burns down to something in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends in' reads as 'turns into', but means the last letters: anthracite ends in these four.
explanation.definitionFit: Cite means quote or refer to, and it is the ending of anthracite.

clue.text: Joined in a dance with Jones.

definitions.text: Joined in a dance with Jones.

parts.words: Joined in a dance with Jones
parts.note: the ... Jones is a ballroom mixer dance where partners change

explanation.surface: Someone takes the floor with a partner named Jones.
explanation.walkthrough: The Paul Jones was a popular party dance in which partners swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul is the first half of the Paul Jones, a ballroom dance.

clue.text: There's wet weather in part of Russia.

definitions.text: There's wet weather in part of Russia.

parts.words: There's wet weather in part of Russia
parts.note: a region then within Soviet Russia whose name holds the word rain

explanation.surface: A weather report of rain in a Russian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer contains RAIN; in 1930 Ukraine was part of the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine was then a Soviet republic, so part of the Russian lands.

clue.text: Donkeys can soon be changed into refreshing fruit.

indicators.note: can soon be changed into says the letters of the fruit may be rearranged

parts.note: oranges are juicy, refreshing citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale transformation turns donkeys into fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect anagram: the letters of ORANGES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of Asia, members of the donkey family.

clue.text: Many women don't change this dress for years.

definitions.text: Many women don't change this dress for years.

parts.words: Many women don't change this dress for years
parts.note: where one lives stays fixed for years, a different sense from clothing

explanation.surface: A comment on women wearing the same frock year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' points to clothing, but the answer is where one lives; ADD + RESS is hidden behind 'this dress'.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is where someone lives, which many keep the same for years.

clue.text: 19 down is both 12 and this.

parts.note: the great waterfall at 19 down is damp (12 down) and throws up spray

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing riddle linking three entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 down is NIAGARA and 12 down is WET; the falls are wet and also sprinkle with spray.
explanation.definitionFit: Splashy means scattering spray, which a great waterfall certainly does.
